provider: Utho Archive Storage (India) — ₹0.38/GB/mo cold tier, ₹-denominated, no egress fee

free_tier.stated: ₹0.38/GB/month, no minimum commitment, 11-nines designed durability, 1-4 hour standard retrieval (instant available). The general object tier is quoted separately at ₹4/GB/month above a 100 GB base.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
per_object_cap.notes: extraction found no per-object clause; some of these providers meter on object count rather than bytes, and some state no cap

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: «No egress fees in India» on the object-storage page and «Zero egress fees» / «No bandwidth overage charges» on the pricing page. The archive page itself says «No hidden retrieval fees». Utho's own pricing API, however, gives no bandwidth allowance per object plan (every plan's `bandwidth` field is 0), so the free-egress claim rests on marketing copy rather than a metered allowance. Record it as a claim, not a contract.

tooling: S3-compatible API with documented REST v2 endpoints (verified live: `GET https://api.utho.com/v2/pricing/objectstorage` -> 200, full plan ladder returned). boto3, rclone `s3`, Datashim. CDN-ready.
chaining: Per-GB with no cap, so 5 TB and 20 TB are the same rate. India-only regions (Noida/Mumbai).
limits_note: 1-4 hour retrieval on the standard path. This is archive, not the hot 10 TiB. The archive product page carries no S3 endpoint of its own and no explicit statement that it is S3-addressable, so it may be a bucket lifecycle class rather than a separate API. Volume pricing is not published: the ladder from the API stops at 10 TB, and 20 TB requires sales contact.
reliability_note: The most important reliability finding here is a PRICE DISCREPANCY INSIDE ONE VENDOR. Utho's marketing pages advertise object storage at «₹4/GB/month above 100 GB» and the pricing-comparison page claims «60-70 % More Affordable Than AWS», while Utho's own plan API returns ₹5.00/GB at 25 GB falling to ₹1.95/GB only at 10 TB. I.e. the advertised headline rate is roughly 2× the actual entry price and only reachable at the top of the ladder. Treat every Utho number as requiring an API cross-check. Node/uptime history not independently verified.

extras.agent_focus: Wave 7 cheap-PAID lane, regional angle: storage sold in RUB / CNY / BRL / INR / ZAR / TRY / PLN / UAH that never appears on Western price lists. Every paid candidate carries price_per_tb_month at USD-converted list price. FX fixed 2026-10-21 from open.er-api.com: RUB 82.5719/USD, CNY 6.6913, BRL 5.0231, INR 94.9952, ZAR 16.3972, TRY 49.5978, PLN 3.8923, UAH 45.0922, EUR 0.89075/USD. Excluded per brief: AWS, Azure, GCP, Alibaba Cloud, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, IDrive e2. Headline result: the true regional floor with genuinely free egress is ~$2.00/TB/mo (Yandex 360 Profi 3 TB on a Russian card) rising to ~$4.17/TB/mo for the same product bought with a foreign card, and ~$5.95-7.56/TB/mo for flat-rate Western-facing file storage (TheHost, Rollin Host). Everything advertised below ~$2/TB/mo in this set is either capacity-capped, egress-metered, or unverifiable marketing.
